title: Sequence steps on a timeline
summary: A timeline groups tweens in order. By default, a new tween begins after the previous one finishes.
introduction: A timeline groups tweens in order. By default, a new tween begins after the previous one finishes. Your task: Swap the last two steps and compare the sequence.
learningObjectives: Swap the last two steps and compare the sequence.

blocks.text: A timeline groups tweens in order. By default, a new tween begins after the previous one finishes.
Use a browser project with GSAP 3 installed. Each example creates its own small box. Run one example at a time with a module build tool. GSAP is not loaded by this site's plain runner.

items: `textContent` reads or replaces plain text inside an element. It does not interpret the supplied words as HTML.
`createElement` makes a new element in memory. Append it to the document when you want it to appear.
A timeline sequences tweens. A position argument can start a step earlier or later than the default end of the previous step.

blocks.text: The box moves, then turns, then fades partway.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Rotation uses degrees in this GSAP CSS example. Do not assume it matches a 3D library's radians.
